_what: ROOT/.container-map/container.json. `python3 cli.py init ROOT` writes one from this file and what it finds on the machine. Every key is optional; paths may start with ~. Optional data sources (digest, relay, dispatch, other machines, the Today screen) are in container.sources-example.json.
name: MYBOX
_theme: the map's theme and texture pack: a file in themes/ (classic, earthen, blueprint, synthwave, phosphor). V in the page cycles them and the browser's choice wins over this.
_skin: the craft, the words on the plates and the wingmate's face: a file in skins/ (neutral ships), or in skins_dir for your own. Fixed per map.
_private: Folder names, or paths inside work_root or absolute ones. A paired phone sees only names and counts for these folders and dot-folders; the local map keeps its file lists.
_hangar_slots: berths on the hangar plate (1-99): agent seats and ships are counted against it, with a warning past it; a display only, nothing is stopped
_agent_verify: false = only the page can attach a verify shell line to a thread; true lets agents (bearer token) do it too. The line runs as you.
_worktree_setup: one shell line a new worktree thread runs before its agent's first run, per repo: {"/abs/path/to/repo": "npm ci", "*": "…"} ("*" = any repo). {} = none. A thread's own setup line wins.
_tick_seconds: the oracle loop's own clock: a failed thread with retries left is sent back every N seconds even with no page open; 0 = off
_constellations: Optional groups for your conversations: [{"name":"Writing", "key":"writing", "keywords":["draft"], "private":false}]. Empty draws no groups unless your scan findings name one. private groups show only a count on phones.
